name: infinite-spiral
title: Infinite Spiral
description: A ring of photo cards arranged along a vertical helix, largest and sharpest at the centre and fading into blur at the edges. It turns on its own and can be paused by hovering.
use: A showcase needs an eye-catching, self-moving wall of images with no controls or captions.
avoid: The images are decorative and hard to click precisely, edge cards blur away, and every frame is drawn continuously.
a11y: Auto rotation stops under reduced motion, but there is no keyboard way to move the spiral and drag is pointer-only. (keyboard: no, labels: good, reduced motion: respected)
looks: A loose column of upright photo cards floats over a near-black stage, each offset and scaled to suggest a helix curving back into space. The central card is biggest and crisp, while cards toward the top and bottom shrink, fade and blur into the dark.
behaves: The helix rotates slowly and continuously, sliding each card along its circular path so different photos drift to the front. Hovering stops the drift, and in drag mode the ring can be pulled by hand.
customise: Items array plus speed, direction, animation mode, helix radius, card size, spacing, perspective, cards per turn, tilt, centre scale, edge fade and blur, hover pause, fit and grayscale are props.
weight: moderate: A requestAnimationFrame loop repositions about a dozen cards every frame.
demo: Nature photos: a lit green valley, a snowy mountain, a red gerbera flower, a leaf and small portraits.
issues: Across the six frames the spiral barely moves, so its endless rotation is hard to read from stills.
polishWhy: Cards and depth read well, but the cluster sits off-centre and much of the stage stays empty.
